title: Investigate and resolve intermittent spikes in per-model usage charts in Console
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Console customers report occasional multi-hour spikes in per-model token/embedding usage charts that do not match raw request logs or billing records. These spikes show up as sharp single-minute buckets that inflate per-model cost attribution. Scope: affects Console charts (per-model breakdown, per-route model view), the usage CSV export, and rollout dashboards for a subset of customers (primarily high-throughput tenants).
description_long:
Problem details:
- Symptom: sudden single-minute spikes in the per-model and per-route views that are not present in the raw request-event export for the same time window. The total token count for account-level reports remains stable, but model-level attribution shows artificial redistribution.
- Initial hypothesis: late-arriving metering events (retries from edge or ingestion Kafka duplicates) are being applied to minute buckets without deduplication, and the aggregation pipeline emits a new minute bucket that overwrote previously-computed sharded aggregates. Alternatively, a race between the real-time summarizer and the hourly rollup can cause double-counting in the Console timeseries when re-emit occurs.
- Impact: customers see misleading per-model cost breakdowns and may misinterpret model quality/cost tradeoffs, and platform teams may incorrectly throttle or change routing policies based on bad telemetry.
- Goal: stop new incorrect spikes within 2 sprints, provide a correction/backfill for affected customers, add monitoring/alerts to detect recurrence, and harden ingestion to prevent duplicates.
comments: 2026-02-20 - Aisha Patel: Triage completed. Reproduced spikes in prod Console for tenant: acme-corp. Spike timestamps: 2026-02-18T14:42Z and 2026-02-19T09:11Z. Raw request logs (edge-proxy) show steady requests; metering topic shows duplicate messages with identical request_id and different ingestion timestamps.

2026-02-22 - Lucas Nguyen: Investigated ingestion. Found that the metering consumer did not persist seen-event ids for a 5-minute window; retries from transient Kafka rebalances reprocessed messages and the aggregator accepted them because it keyed only on minute+model. Added temporary dedupe filter in the summarizer which reduced spikes in test cluster.

2026-02-25 - Lucas Nguyen: Deployed hotfix on staging: idempotency table (in Redis) for (tenant,request_id) with 24-hour TTL. Staging run for 72h shows no duplicate buckets for previously failing tenants. Next: evaluate scaling/cost of Redis dedupe under high throughput (10k reqs/s).

2026-03-02 - Performance note (Maya Thompson): Redis dedupe introduced ~0.6ms median additional latency per metering write and ~3% extra throughput requirement. For committed Dedicated customers we prefer a sharded in-process LRU dedupe followed by persistent watermarking in ClickHouse. Proposal linked: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Idempotent+Metering+Design

2026-03-04 - Decision: Follow two-phase plan: 1) Short-term: keep Redis dedupe + make aggregator emit monotonic counters per (tenant,model,minute) so re-emits are idempotent; 2) Long-term: move dedupe to the ingest layer using a partitioned CausalID table written to ClickHouse with TTL. Created tech-spec PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1428

2026-03-07 - QA: Added integration test that replays a production trace with duplicate events and asserts that per-model minute buckets are unchanged after dedupe. Test added to inference/integration/fixtures - Jenkins job green.

2026-03-10 - Ops (Javier Morales): Backfill plan drafted. Backfill will: 1) identify affected minute buckets using mismatches between raw-events and aggregated-timeseries, 2) recompute aggregation using deduped raw events, 3) patch Console-timeseries and CSV exports. Expect ~12 hours of CPU for a high-volume tenant. Backfill script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tools/blob/main/backfill-metering/repair_duplicates.py

2026-03-12 - Lucas Nguyen: Deployed aggregator change to prod (feature-flagged). Enabled dedupe for 3 medium tenants for monitoring. No new spikes observed in 48h. Next steps: roll out to all tenants behind a rollout schedule; create alerting for minute-level outliers and for divergence of (sum per-model) vs (account total).
